comparator.name: Bachelor Life Science and Technology
comparator.sourceNotes: The official 2026-2027 Teaching and Examination Regulations define one 180-EC Life Science and Technology major, with 60 EC in each year. The complete compulsory first- and second-year curricula are reproduced below at their exact component-credit level. The third year preserves the regulated 30-EC minor, 15-EC bachelor research project and 15 EC of approved major electives. The programme does not define named tracks, so no route is selected and the restricted third-year elective space is not converted into an invented specialisation.

exception.reason: The University of Groningen programme is an integrated life-science, chemistry, physics and experimental-technology degree. Its compulsory spine joins mammalian cell biology, biochemistry, physiology, genetics and evolution with a two-course organic-chemistry sequence, pharmaceutical analysis, bioinorganic chemistry, optics, thermodynamics, biophysics, quantum and classical mechanics, imaging and spectroscopy. That theory is reinforced by dedicated practical courses in optics and cell biology, microbiology and organic chemistry, then by applied microbiology, applied biotechnology and a 15-EC research project. UCR offers meaningful molecular biology, biochemistry, physiology, genetics, pharmacology, laboratory, calculus, linear-algebra, programming and data-science courses. It does not offer the chemistry, physics, imaging, spectroscopy, microbiology, biotechnology and staged laboratory progression that defines this degree. A UCR programme built from the closest available courses would be a credible molecular-biomedicine pathway, but it would not be a defensible Life Science and Technology comparator.
exception.curriculumContext: The official 2026-2027 regulations account for the full 180 EC. Year one comprises twelve 5-EC courses spanning optics, mammalian cell biology, an optics-and-cell-biology practical, organic chemistry, biochemistry, calculus, programming, thermodynamics, physiology, pharmaceutical analysis, biophysics and scientific communication. Year two comprises twelve further 5-EC courses in applied microbiology, linear algebra, a microbiology practical, bioinorganic chemistry, quantum and classical mechanics, imaging, advanced organic chemistry, spectroscopy, an organic-chemistry practical, genetics and evolution, applied biotechnology, and professional ethics. Year three comprises a 30-EC minor, 15 EC of approved Life Science and Technology electives and a 15-EC bachelor research project. The live programme page likewise presents the degree as a multidisciplinary integration of biology, chemistry, physics, pharmaceutical science, technology and informatics.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed all 151 current enriched UCR workbook rows, including descriptions, outline-derived profiles, disciplines, topics, methods, prerequisites and planned Fall 2026 cohort terms. HCBGATE101 Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine, HCBLIFE211 Molecular Cell Biology, HCBLIFE213 Biochemistry, HCBLIFE212 Human Physiology and HCBLIFE311 Molecular Pathology & Genetics provide strong foundations in cells, biomolecules, metabolism, physiology and genetics. HCBLIFE214 Life Science Laboratory adds biochemical and molecular laboratory work, including bacterial techniques, GMOs, protein production, DNA analysis and basic bioinformatics. HCBBIOM311 Pharmacology, HCBBIOM312 Infection & Immunity and HCBBIOM313 Mechanisms of Disease extend drugs, microbes, immunity and disease. DISGATE101 Introduction to Programming, DISGATE102 Mathematical Methods, DISMATH211 Linear Algebra, DISMATH214 Advanced Calculus, DISMATH314 Probability & Statistics and DISDATA211 Machine Learning support programming and quantitative analysis. The workbook nevertheless contains no organic-chemistry sequence, pharmaceutical-analysis course, bioinorganic chemistry, dedicated optics sequence, thermodynamics course, quantum or classical mechanics for life sciences, spectroscopy sequence, dedicated biomedical imaging course, applied-microbiology sequence, applied-biotechnology course, or practical organic-chemistry course. HCBLIFE214 is a valuable single introductory laboratory course, but it cannot replace the target programme's staged optics and cell-biology, microbiology and organic-chemistry practical formation. The available UCR courses also do not culminate in an equivalent 15-EC experimental research project integrating this chemistry-physics-technology spine. The closest UCR combination therefore covers biological and computational foundations while leaving the target's defining chemistry, physics, instrumentation, biotechnology and advanced laboratory formation unmatched.
